System Architecture The provided functional decomposition serves to illustrate SCCOUT’s overall purpose and the subdivisions of tasks which make this possible. The goal is to survey user-defined target areas. This involves interactions between subtasks including mapping, classification of visuals, application of chemicals, and user I/O. Figure 11: Functional Decomposition Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory 24 LLNL-TR-2004679 To further explain the connections between the subprocesses listed in the functional decomposition, a functional architecture diagram is given in Figure 12. Most relations in this diagram are feed-forward, but there is a feedback loop between the mapping and visual identification blocks. This loop exists because not all images created during mapping will be saved. All images are analyzed to determine if they contain one or more target species. If so, GPS location, image, and image classification will be logged. Else, image data and location will not be saved or mapped. The functional architecture also highlights the importance of front-end support via the operator tablet and back-end support via the docking drone and remote server. Risk Assessment Three distinct risks to successful implementation and operation of SCCOUT are discussed. Plans for risk mitigation and metrics for risk assessment are also laid out. 1. Chemical Spills: physical vulnerabilities in the sprayer tank or plumbing resulting in a leak of pesticide/herbicide. Could result from material degradation, material incompatibility, or bumps and falls. a) Likelihood: Medium b) Consequence: Medium High c) Mitigation: I. Conduct fall tests on the drones carrying chemical solutions to incorporate engineering solutions to address falls II. Conduct annual leak testing on deployed systems III. Perform material compatibility tests on tanks and plumbing for each chemical approved for use with SCCOUT IV. Implement software interlocks to allow only approved chemicals with compatible tanks and plumbing as per the above bullet d) Technical Performance Measures: I. Record the number of incidents of chemical spills II. Measure the volume of spilled chemicals e) Risk Profile: The change of risk profile due to risk mitigation actions is shown in Figure 13 Figure 13 Chemical Spill Risk Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory 26 LLNL-TR-2004679 2.
